channel.title: Cutroom Notes
channel.description: Work notes on video editing, AI and automation.

item.title: How my Naver blog input tool stopped needing a PC folder and local server and started reading from GitHub
item.description: When I handed Claude a Naver migration, it rewrote the input tool that needed a PC folder and a local server so that it reads drafts and photos straight from GitHub. Now all the PC has to provide is one logged-in Whale browser window.

item.title: I made the film for our wedding ceremony with Higgsfield: how to describe a scene to AI
item.description: I made the film played in the middle of our wedding ceremony with Higgsfield. What took longest was not generating video but describing each scene to the AI precisely.

item.title: Want to join Coupang's reviewer program but stuck with dozens of overdue reviews? Try this
item.description: I gave only keywords for 20 Coupang reviews: Claude directed the work, Gemini wrote the text, and Claude posted it. Here are the failures and the order that finally worked.

item.title: Tired of re-explaining every new Claude chat, I built an AI brain on GitHub
item.description: To get the same result no matter which device or chat window I use, I moved my rules and progress into a GitHub repository outside Claude. After a week of attempts, a new window now picks up the work from a single phrase: “connect blog”.

item.title: Making a wedding-prep checklist by exporting our KakaoTalk chat and handing it to Claude
item.description: I exported the whole KakaoTalk chat with my wife from our wedding prep, gave it to Claude, and got a web checklist split into done and not done that we could tick off together.

item.title: Residents are blocking data centers, so who is laughing?
item.description: Residents are the ones blocking data centers, but I think the ones who gain more the more they are blocked are the companies that already own data centers.

item.title: The AI ad model is way too handsome: jumping in early, in the age of “AI? Fun is enough”
item.description: We've reached the point where people hit 2.44 million hearts on an AI video, and my company got on that wave early and is making ads with AI models.

item.title: Claiming languages first: I turned the idea into a multilingual site the same day
item.description: The idea of claiming the still-empty languages first, I turned into a site in Indonesian, Hindi and Arabic on the very same day. AI turns what used to stay an idea into action.

item.title: Before content floods in endlessly, I should claim the languages that are still empty
item.description: After watching the 30 minutes it took to post one article shrink to almost nothing, I felt I should claim a place in the languages where AI adoption lags before content floods in, and that it had to be done now.

item.title: Subtitling 62 hours of travel footage, and working efficiently with AI
item.description: For 62 hours of travel footage, I changed the subtitle workflow: Premiere's transcription finds where people speak, and only the highlights get polished with Gemini. With AI, the cost turned out to depend on conversation length and the number of back-and-forths.

item.title: Writing on a Naver blog with AI: fully automated up to saving the draft
item.description: Uploading to a Naver blog used to take me over 30 minutes by hand each time. Now AI drives the browser directly, puts in the text, photos, captions and title, and saves it as a draft.

item.title: Opening this blog
item.description: The opening post of my Korean-language personal blog, where I keep my work process, thoughts and everyday life in one place.

item.title: Letting AI drive Premiere directly: notes on setting up the Premiere MCP
item.description: I connected the Claude desktop app and a Premiere MCP so AI could operate my PC and Premiere directly, and worked through the installation traps and port fights one by one.

item.title: Syncing capture times across five cameras and building per-day sequences in Premiere
item.description: I lined up 905 clips from cameras with mismatched clocks to their real capture times using GPS and photos, then automatically built per-day Premiere sequences with a separate track for each camera.

item.title: Backing up travel footage: I left it to AI overnight and got a verification report in the morning
item.description: Footage from a trip to Tanzania was scattered across several cameras and hard drives. I let AI consolidate it onto one drive overnight, and in the morning I had a report that checked every file against its source.
